objective:
Add named profiles to the INI settings file, so one file can serve several deployments. Besides the section `[stockroom]`, the file may hold sections `[stockroom:NAME]`, one per profile. A profile is chosen with the new global option `--profile NAME` or with the environment variable `STOCKROOM_PROFILE`; the option wins over the variable. An empty name, from the option or from the variable, means that no profile is chosen, so `--profile ""` switches off a profile that the variable names. `STOCKROOM_PROFILE` is not a setting: it needs no setting key and is never an error.

Without a chosen profile everything works as before and the `[stockroom:NAME]` sections are ignored completely (their keys are not even validated). With a chosen profile:
- The settings come from the defaults, then `[stockroom]` (which may be missing), then the profile section, then the `STOCKROOM_<KEY>` environment variables, each overriding the one before. A profile section overrides only the keys that are written in that profile section itself. As today, keys of a `[DEFAULT]` section count as keys of `[stockroom]` (when that section exists) and they are not copied into profile sections.
- The section name is matched exactly and case-sensitively: `[stockroom:dev]` is the profile `dev`, while `[Stockroom:dev]`, `[stockroom: dev]`, `[stockroom-dev]` and `[stockroom:dev ]` are not profiles. A profile name may contain any characters that can appear in a section name, for example `prod-eu`, `a.b`, `x y` or `a:b`.
- The keys and values of a profile section are validated like those of `[stockroom]`: an unknown key or a bad value (a `tax_bp` that is not a non-negative whole number, a boolean that is not a boolean) ends the command with exit code 1 and the one usual error line; for an unknown key the line contains the key and the header text `[stockroom:NAME]`.
- A chosen profile that the file does not define, and a chosen profile when no `--config` file is given, end the command with exit code 1 and one `stockroom: error: ` line that contains the profile name. Stdout stays empty in every error case.

Nothing else changes: other commands, the settings file format without profiles and the error messages for problems outside profiles keep their behaviour.
acceptance: --profile NAME applies the keys of [stockroom:NAME] on top of [stockroom]: a profile that sets currency_symbol and low_stock_warning changes price output and the warning of stock, keys it does not set keep the [stockroom] value, and the [stockroom] section may be absent
STOCKROOM_PROFILE chooses a profile when the option is absent, the option wins over the variable, an empty option value switches the variable's profile off, and an empty variable means no profile
STOCKROOM_<KEY> environment variables override the profile's values; STOCKROOM_PROFILE itself is never reported as an unknown setting
Without a chosen profile, or for profile sections that are not chosen, [stockroom:*] sections are not validated (a bad key or value there is no error)
Section names are matched exactly and case-sensitively ([Stockroom:dev], [stockroom: dev], [stockroom-dev], [stockroom:dev ] are not profiles); names with '-', '.', spaces and ':' work
Keys of [DEFAULT] apply to [stockroom] as before and are not copied into a profile section, so a profile without the key keeps the [stockroom] value

An unknown key or a bad value in the chosen profile, a profile that is not defined, and a profile without --config each give exit code 1, empty stdout and one 'stockroom: error: ' line (naming the key and '[stockroom:NAME]', or the profile name)
Runs without profiles behave exactly as before, and --profile without a value is a usage error (exit 2)
